front: When did the Hungarian Rising begin?
When did Soviet forces crush the Hungarian Rising?
back: From 4 November 1956; Kádár installed, Nagy executed in 1958.

front: When did the Warsaw Pact invade Czechoslovakia?

back: Dubček's reforms in Czechoslovakia in 1968, ended by the Warsaw Pact invasion.
Soviet claim (1968) of a right to intervene in any communist state where communism was threatened.
Khrushchev's criticism of Stalin's crimes from 1956 and easing of some harsh policies.

front: Why did the USSR crush Hungary in 1956?
back: Nagy announced free elections and that Hungary would leave the Warsaw Pact.

front: Main difference between Nagy and Dubček?
back: Nagy took Hungary out of the Warsaw Pact; Dubček promised to stay in it.

front: Why did the West not help Hungary in 1956?
back: It would not risk war with the USSR, and the Suez Crisis divided and distracted the West.
